snapshot.summary:
- Purpose: e-commerce demo storefront for browsing products, viewing details, adding items to a cart, and accessing related resources (signup/login, API/testing guides, contact, tutorials).
- Primary user flows: browse by category/brand, open product detail (View Product), add items to cart (Add to cart → View Cart), signup/login, navigate site header links (Home, Products, Contact us, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials).
- Secondary flows: filter/list products by gender/section (WOMEN, MEN, KIDS) and brand, use header navigation to reach APIs and learning resources.
- Important UI interactions: product list pagination/counts, view product modal/page, cart update and navigation to checkout.
- Key data flows: session/cart persistence across pages and after login; signup/login state changes available actions.
- Edge cases to test: adding same item multiple times, quantity limits/validation, adding out-of-stock or removed products, cart persistence after logout or across sessions, concurrent cart updates from multiple tabs.
- Robustness checks: malformed inputs on signup/login, slow/failed network or JS disabled, broken links for header resources, and responsive layout/menu behavior on mobile.

snapshot.summary:
- Main purpose: display the full product catalogue so users can browse categories/brands, view product details, and add items to the shopping cart.  
- Primary user flows: navigate site header (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Contact), filter by category/brand, open "View Product" for details, use "Add to cart" from listing or detail, then "View Cart" to checkout; access account pages via Signup/Login.  
- Secondary flows: scroll-to-top (#scrollUp), explore video/API/testing/test-cases links, and category navigation for WOMEN/MEN/KIDS submenus.  
- Key UI actions to test: category/brand filters, product list pagination/loading, product detail display, add-to-cart behavior, view-cart navigation, and login-required behavior for account/cart persistence.  
- Edge case — cart/quantity: adding same item multiple times, rapid repeated clicks, zero/negative quantity inputs, cart persistence across sessions and after login/logout.  
- Edge case — data/display: missing or broken images, malformed product names/prices, inconsistent counts (category count vs shown items), out-of-stock or unavailable products.  
- Edge case — navigation/resilience: deep links to product pages, browser back/forward, slow networks/timeouts, and JS-disabled behavior.  
- Edge case — concurrency/security: inventory changes during checkout, price tampering in client, session expiration during purchase.

snapshot.summary:
- Main purpose: allow users to create an account or sign in (Signup / Login) and offer related navigation (Home, Products, Cart, Test Cases, Contact) and a newsletter subscription.
- Main user flows: create new account (signup), authenticate existing user (login), subscribe to newsletter (email input + #subscribe), navigate to other site sections via top links, use #scrollUp to jump to top.
- Primary interactive controls: Login and Signup buttons, newsletter input (#susbscribe_email) + subscribe button, several top navigation links.
- Expected input fields: likely name, email, password and other signup/login fields (multiple input elements detected).
- Important edge cases — validation: empty fields, invalid email formats, too-short/too-long passwords, leading/trailing whitespace, Unicode/special characters.
- Important edge cases — duplicate/already-registered email on signup, incorrect credentials, account lockout/rate-limit, case-sensitivity of email/password.
- Security/robustness edge cases: SQL injection/XSS payloads, CSRF, session handling after login/logout, unsecured redirects.
- UI/UX edge cases: disabled/hidden states, duplicate or misspelled element IDs (e.g., "susbscribe_email"), link targets/misroutes, responsiveness and keyboard/accessibility support, and behavior under slow/no network.

snapshot.summary:
- Main purpose: display the shopping cart contents and let users proceed to checkout or continue shopping from the Cart (URL /view_cart).
- Main user flows: review cart items (quantities, prices), remove/update items, proceed to checkout (may require login), navigate to Home/Products/Contact/Test Cases/API/Video pages via header links.
- Secondary flow: subscribe to newsletter via email input (#susbscribe_email) and Subscribe button (#subscribe); use ScrollUp control to jump to top.
- Navigation flows: header links ("Home", "Products", "Cart", "Signup / Login", etc.) should route correctly; "here" link likely context-specific (e.g., login/register).
- Important data/UX edge cases: empty cart view, removing the last item, zero/negative/very large quantity inputs, and price/total recalculation errors.
- Session/state edge cases: cart persistence across login/logout, session expiration during checkout, and correct redirect after login when continuing checkout.
- Input validation/security: invalid or malicious newsletter email (format, XSS), disabled/duplicate subscribe submissions, and resilience to slow/failed network responses.
- Link and element robustness: broken header links, missing product images or details, and accessibility/responsiveness on different viewports.

snapshot.summary:
- Purpose: a "Contact Us" page for users to send feedback/messages and subscribe to a newsletter, plus site navigation links.
- Main flows: navigate via top links (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials, Contact us); submit contact form (name/email/subject/message); subscribe with email (#susbscribe_email); use scroll-up control.
- Form elements: multiple input fields and a textarea (#message); subscribe button (#subscribe).
- Expected validations: required fields, email format for contact and subscribe, subject/message length limits.
- Success/error handling: confirmation messages, field-level errors, and server-side validation must display correctly.
- Edge inputs: empty submissions, invalid email formats, extremely long text, leading/trailing whitespace, unicode/emoji, and special characters (XSS/SQL injection vectors).
- Interaction edge cases: double submissions, slow/failed network, JS disabled (no client validation), and incorrect/missing element IDs (e.g., typo #susbscribe_email).
- Accessibility/responsive: keyboard navigation, focus order, ARIA labels, and layout on different screen sizes and browsers.
